record.excerpt: 1. Bitcoin Trend Score > 7 … 2. Bitcoin Relative Trend Score > 7 … 3. Bitcoin closed at a 10-day high … 1. Bitcoin Trend Score falls below 5 … Entry conditions require simultaneous triggers, whereas exit conditions act independently. … Since 2011, the trend score system has generated ten buy signals with a 70% success rate, achieving an average gain of 1436.28% per win, while losses averaged -18.78%.
record.performance_claim: ten buy signals with a 70% success rate
record.notes: Looks mechanical but relies on proprietary undefined Trend Score indicators; only the 10-day-high leg is computable. Good trap: compiler should flag unresolvable inputs.

spec.claim_summary: A Bitcoin long strategy enters when Trend Score and Relative Trend Score both exceed 7 with price at a 10-day high and exits when Trend Score falls below 5.
spec.untestable_reason: The entry and exit depend on the proprietary Bitcoin Trend Score and Relative Trend Score which cannot be expressed with the available indicators.

claimed.other: average gain of 1436.28% per win, while losses averaged -18.78%

assumptions: Asset is Bitcoin mapped to BTCUSDT.
Timeframe 1d chosen from page chart timeframe; not stated by claimant.
Direction long inferred from buy signals.

NOT EXPRESSIBLE: Bitcoin Trend Score and Bitcoin Relative Trend Score are proprietary scores with no definition in available indicators; entry requires both >7 and exit requires Trend Score <5, which is the heart of the strategy.
Entry 10-day high compiled as close > previous 10-bar highest_high.
Exit has no expressible core because the only stated exit uses the proprietary Trend Score.
